subject: humanities
passage: In villages of West Bengal, in eastern India, painters known as patuas have long made scrolls called pats: strips of cloth-backed paper several meters long, painted in bright natural colors with the scenes of a single story. A pat was never meant to hang silently on a wall. <u>The patua carried it from house to house, unrolling one frame at a time while singing a song composed to match the pictures.</u> The painting and the song were made together, and a scroll without its singer is, in the patuas' view, only half a work. Today many patuas also sell their scrolls to collectors, but the songs still travel with them.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It describes the materials from which a pat is made.
choices.B: It suggests that patuas no longer perform their scrolls.
choices.C: It explains how a scroll was traditionally presented, supporting the claim that it was not meant to hang silently.
choices.D: It argues that the songs are more important than the paintings.

explanation.why: The sentence before the underlined one makes a claim: a pat "was never meant to hang silently on a wall." The underlined sentence shows what was done with it instead, carried from house to house and unrolled while the patua sang. It supports the claim by describing the traditional performance.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The materials are described in the first sentence; the underlined sentence is about performance.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The underlined sentence describes the traditional performance, and the final sentence says the songs "still travel" with the scrolls.
explanation.C: Correct. By describing the house-to-house performance with song, the sentence backs up the preceding claim that a pat was not meant to hang silently.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says painting and song were "made together" and treats them as two halves of one work; it does not rank them.
